keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the 299-849 Maya envelope covers Naranjo). The page gives only the site: 'at least 8 km2', centre 'about 2.25 km2', '389 recorded buildings in the central area'; no kingdom extent or tributaries (Holmul is 'subordinate' to Naranjo c. 600). Drawn as a nominal 20 km disc (about 1,260 km2, five grid cells), soft.

ledger.note: 546: the first dated ruler, Ah Wosaaj Chan K'inich, comes to power: 'Not much is known about the site before the ruler Ah Wosaaj Chan K'inich who came to power in 546 AD.' The site was occupied 'from about 500 BC' and its founding is mythical.

region.text: Naranjo (Sa'aal), 'about 50 km east of the site of Tikal' along the Mopan and Holmul rivers; 'at least 8 km2' with the urban centre about 2.25 km2

ledger.note: 546: 'Naranjo came under the control of Calakmul whose ruler Tuun Kab Hix appointed Ah Wosaaj Chan K'inich', 'a deliberate move by Calakmul to take allies away from Tikal'.

region.text: Naranjo (Sa'aal), 'about 50 km east of the site of Tikal' along the Mopan and Holmul rivers; 'at least 8 km2' with the urban centre about 2.25 km2

ledger.note: 626: page silent on Naranjo leaving Calakmul; 'In 626 two attacks were made on Naranjo by Caracol' and Naranjo 'was then retaken by Calakmul in 631', which implies a lapse of Calakmul's control.

ledger.note: 631: 'Naranjo was then retaken by Calakmul in 631.' In 682 Calakmul sent Lady Six Sky 'to reestablish the dynasty'.

ledger.note: About 695: page silent on any end to Calakmul's hold after 631; the date is a bridge placed in the 693-698 attacks, when Naranjo is recorded acting on its own account ('defeating Tikal in 695 AD').

region.text: Naranjo (Sa'aal), 'about 50 km east of the site of Tikal' along the Mopan and Holmul rivers; 'at least 8 km2' with the urban centre about 2.25 km2

ledger.note: 810: 'Naranjo's final abandonment may have been the result of political turmoil and a severe drought dated to 810 AD'; the last dated text is Altar 2 of 790. The site was 'occupied from about 500 BC to 950 AD'.

wars.name: Caracol-Naranjo star wars

zones.text: Naranjo (Sa'aal), 'about 50 km east of the site of Tikal' along the Mopan and Holmul rivers; 'at least 8 km2' with the urban centre about 2.25 km2

wars.outcome: Two Caracol attacks in 626; Calakmul retook Naranjo in 631; Naranjo defeated Caracol in an undated 'star war' under K'ahk' Xiiw Chan Chaahk; 'by 680 Caracol had apparently recovered and eliminated K'ahk' Xiiw'. Lady Six Sky came from Calakmul in 682.
wars.note: The Caracol page (see caracol dossier) records Caracol winning a star war on Naranjo in 631 and Naranjo independent in 680; the pages disagree on who held Naranjo between 631 and 680.

wars.name: Naranjo's wars on Tikal, Ucanal and Yaxha
wars.outcome: 'Between 693 and 698 AD Naranjo carried out a series of at least eight attacks', 'defeating Tikal in 695 AD and Ucanal in 698 AD'; another series from 706 'including the defeat of Yaxha in 710'. No land change is recorded.

wars.name: Tikal's defeat of Naranjo
wars.outcome: 'Naranjo was defeated by Tikal in 744 AD and the ruler, Yax Mayuy Chan Chaak, was taken captive and likely sacrificed.' No land change is recorded.

sources.title: Naranjo (Maya site)
sources.note: Sa'aal / Wak Kab'nal: 546 Calakmul control, 626 Caracol attacks, 631 retaken by Calakmul, 680 Caracol, 682 Lady Six Sky, 693-710 attacks, 744 Tikal, 810 drought. At least 8 km2.

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Naranjo row. The page has no infobox.
DISAGREEMENTS. Caracol page (caracol dossier): Caracol wins a star war on Naranjo in 631 and Naranjo wins independence in 680. Naranjo page: Caracol attacks twice in 626, Calakmul retakes Naranjo in 631, Caracol 'eliminated K'ahk' Xiiw' by 680, Calakmul sends Lady Six Sky in 682. Calakmul page (calakmul dossier): 546 enthronement, free 'by at least 626'. The vassal_end of 695 is a bridge; no page opened dates the end of Calakmul's hold.
START AND END. 546 is the first dated ruler, not the founding (occupied from about 500 BC; founding mythical); 810 is the page's drought-linked abandonment 'may have been'.
COORDINATES. The page prints none; the 20 km disc is centred on a point 50 km east of Tikal's gazetteer coordinates. Naranjo, Yaxha, Ucanal and Holmul lie east of Tikal; their dossiers do not exist (Yaxha and Ucanal are named as victims in 698 and 710; Holmul as subordinate c. 600). Gazetteer lacks 'Naranjo' and 'Sa'aal'.
